title: Hacker Runs Hermes AI Agent Unattended for Post-Exploitation at Thai Finance Ministry

reading.body:
An AI agent called Hermes was deployed by an attacker to conduct autonomous network reconnaissance against Thailand's Ministry of Finance without human oversight. The system was used for post-exploitation activities after the attacker had already compromised ministry networks, suggesting it was applied to tasks beyond initial access. This represents a failure to detect and stop an unattended AI system operating inside a sensitive government network during the window when it was active.

The attack combined a custom Go implant called Hades with the autonomous AI agent to access administrative systems, email infrastructure, and big data platforms. Researchers discovered the attacker's staging server with exploit code and stolen credentials only after the operation had concluded. What would have caught this is network monitoring that flagged unusual autonomous agent activity during the compromise period, or detection of the staging infrastructure before the Hermes agent was deployed.

It is not established what specific reconnaissance tasks Hermes performed, how long it operated undetected, or what data exfiltration occurred as a result of the agent's activities.

summary:
# Summary

Thailand's Ministry of Finance was targeted in a cyberattack from mid to late June through mid-July 2026. Researchers discovered three exposed directories on a Hong Kong server containing 585 files and 470 MB of attack materials, including exploit code, webshells, and stolen credentials. The attackers deployed a custom Go implant called Hades and used an AI agent named Hermes to autonomously conduct network reconnaissance without human oversight. Evidence suggests the operator successfully compromised multiple ministry systems and accessed session cookies from administrative panels, Hadoop infrastructure, GlassFish servers, and email systems.

The attack involved a Chinese-speaking operator using sophisticated custom tools targeting the ministry's financial systems and big data infrastructure. Researchers identified four servers across Hong Kong and Malaysia linked to the operation through shared certificates and malware communications. The staging server hosted 62 malware variants disguised as legitimate system processes, privilege escalation exploits, and specialized scripts for exploiting Hadoop clusters. Thailand's national security agencies were notified on July 15, 2026, and acknowledged receipt the same day before the findings were published.
